away.name: Darcy Kuemper
away.news: Kuemper has been far from stellar this season, but through 18 games, he remains the only goalie with a win for the Kings. The 36-year-old Kuemper has allowed eight goals on 38 shots (.789 SV%) in his last two games (0-2-0) and has allowed three or more goals in four of his last five (3-2-0). The Kings enter Tuesday's game as +136 road underdogs against a Boston Bruins team that has been outscored 11-4 during a two-game losing streak (0-2-0).

home.name: Michael DiPietro
home.news: Jeremy Swayman has been solid for the Boston Bruins this season, stealing some of the attention from rookie Michael DiPietro, who has been excellent in limited action. The 27-year-old DiPietro has a stellar 1.98 GAA and .931 SV% in his last five appearances (4-0-0). That said, he has only started one game in the past two and a half weeks, a 17-save performance (.895 SV%) in a 6-2 win over the Pittsburgh Penguins. The Bruins enter Tuesday's game as -146 home favourites against a struggling Los Angeles Kings team that has scored just six goals during a four-game losing streak (0-4-0).

away.name: Logan Thompson
away.news: Thompson will start Tuesday in Tampa.

home.name: Andrei Vasilevskiy
home.news: Vasilevskiy, the reigning Vezina Trophy winner, has been far from stellar this season. That said, he played well in his most recent outing, saving 20 of 21 shots (.952 SV%), but his team let him down in a 2-0 loss to the Detroit Red Wings. The 32-year-old goalie has uncharacteristically allowed three or more goals in nine of 15 games this season (9-5-1). Still, Tampa Bay enters Tuesday's game as -154 home favourites against a Washington Capitals team that has been outscored 12-6 in their past two games (0-2-0).

away.name: Devon Levi
away.news: For the first time in years, the Oilers are seeing reliable goaltending night in, night out, with Devon Levi leading the way. The 24-year-old Levi is coming off his first career shutout, a 19-save performance in a 1-0 win over the Toronto Maple Leafs. Since returning from a two-week absence with a lower-body injury, Levi has been outstanding, saving 70 of 73 shots (.959 SV%) in three games (3-0-0). The Oilers enter Tuesday's outing as slight +108 road underdogs against a Florida Panthers team with points in four straight games (3-0-1).

home.name: Jacob Markstrom
home.news: Markstrom was minutes away from his second shutout of the season in his most recent outing, a 24-save performance (.960 SV%) in a 4-1 win over the St. Louis Blues. The 36-year-old Markstrom has been tough to beat lately, saving 62 of 64 shots (.969 SV%) in his last two games (2-0-0). That said, Markstrom will have a tough task on Tuesday against an Edmonton Oilers team on a five-game win streak. The Panthers enter Tuesday's contest as -118 home favourites.

away.name: Cam Talbot
away.news: Jet Greaves was expected to lead the way between the pipes for Columbus this season, but early-season struggles have given Talbot more ice time. That said, Greaves' struggles aside, Talbot has played well lately and earned his share of starts. The veteran 39-year-old goalie has been excellent in recent games, posting a 1.98 GAA and .930 SV% in his last seven appearances (4-2-0). The Blue Jackets enter Tuesday's contest as +126 road underdogs against a New York Islanders team that has outscored opponents 11-4 in their past two games (2-0-0).

home.name: Ilya Sorokin
home.news: After establishing himself as an elite goalie in his first three seasons, Sorokin has posted mid-pack statistics for three consecutive seasons. That said, the 31-year-old goalie is off to a strong start in 2026-27, performing better under new Head Coach Pete DeBoer. Sorokin was solid in his most recent outing, saving 26 of 28 shots (.929 SV%) in a 5-2 win over the Los Angeles Kings. The Islanders enter Tuesday's game as -139 home favourites against a Columbus Blue Jackets team that has scored two or fewer goals in three of their past four games (0-4-0).

away.name: Alex Lyon
away.news: The Sabres have struggled to get adequate goaltending all season and will continue to roll with Lyon between the pipes for a third consecutive game after making his season debut following a lengthy upper-body injury. The 33-year-old Lyon has yet to win (0-1-1) but has played well in both outings, posting a 2.48 GAA and .909 SV%. He was especially strong in Saturday's 2-0 loss to the Dallas Stars, saving 28 of 30 shots (.933 SV%). The Sabres enter Tuesday's contest as -123 road favourites against a Philadelphia Flyers team coming off a 5-2 loss to the Edmonton Oilers.

home.name: Joseph Woll
home.news: Woll has lost eight of 11 games this season (3-6-2), but has given the Flyers a chance to win on most nights, posting a serviceable 2.92 GAA and .902 SV%. That said, Woll is coming off consecutive wins, saving 47 of 51 combined shots (.922 SV%) and will return to the crease for the third time in five games. The Flyers enter Tuesday's game as +110 home underdogs against a Buffalo Sabres team that has scored only six goals during a four-game losing streak (0-3-1).

away.name: Sergei Bobrovsky
away.news: When the Maple Leafs signed Bobrovsky to a three-year, $7 million AAV contract ($21M total) in the offseason, the hope was that he could solidify their crease and return the team to the postseason. That said, Bobrovsky has struggled to start his tenure with the Maple Leafs, posting an ugly 3.47 GAA and .881 SV% in 13 games (3-8-2). Even more alarming, Bobrovsky has allowed three or more goals in all but one of his 13 outings. The veteran 38-year-old goalie hopes to snap a five-game losing streak on Tuesday, as the Maple Leafs enter action as -146 road favourites against the league's worst offence, the Chicago Blackhawks (2.3 GF/GP).

home.name: Spencer Knight
home.news: After a promising inaugural full season with the Blackhawks in 2025-26, posting a 2.82 GAA and .902 SV% in 55 games (19-25-11), Knight has had an inconsistent start to 2026-27. In his most recent game, he allowed four goals on 31 shots (.871 SV%) in a 5-4 shootout loss to the Winnipeg Jets. The 25-year-old American goalie has allowed four or more goals in four of his last five games (1-3-1). The Blackhawks enter Tuesday's game as +133 home underdogs against a struggling Toronto Maple Leafs team that is desperately trying to snap a six-game losing streak (0-6-0).

home.name: Jordan Binnington
home.news: After a career-worst 2025-26 season, posting a 3.33 GAA and .873 SV% in 41 games (13-20-7), Binnington has struggled to start 2026-27, taking a clear backseat to Joel Hofer. The 33-year-old Binnington has only had one quality start in five games this season (1-3-0) and has allowed five or more goals three times. The Blues enter Tuesday's game as -128 home favourites against the Anaheim Ducks, who are coming off an explosive 6-1 win over the Calgary Flames.

home.name: Jesper Wallstedt
home.news: Wallstedt has deservedly been the busiest goalie in the NHL this season, playing 19 of 22 games, posting a tremendous 1.94 GAA and .926 SV% with a 14-2-3 record. The 23-year-old Swedish goalie was excellent in Minnesota's previous game, saving 31 of 33 shots (.939 SV%) in a 6-2 win over the Boston Bruins. With Filip Gustavsson (hip) nearing his season debut, Wallstedt will likely see a slightly lighter workload, but he has proven himself as one of the NHL's best goalies on any given night. Minnesota enters Tuesday's game as -196 home favourites against a Nashville Predators team whose seven-game winning streak was snapped on Sunday in a 4-2 loss to the San Jose Sharks.

away.name: Linus Ullmark
away.news: Ullmark missed nearly three weeks with a lower-body injury, but hasn't missed a step since returning, continuing a tremendous start to the 2026-27 season. The 33-year-old Swedish goalie was solid in his most recent outing, saving 16 of 17 shots (.941 SV%) in a 4-1 win over the Pittsburgh Penguins. Ullmark has allowed two or fewer goals in all but one of 10 games this season (9-1-0). The Senators enter Tuesday's game as -131 road favourites against a red-hot Winnipeg Jets team that has scored four or more goals in six consecutive games (6-0-0).

home.name: Stuart Skinner
home.news: After a nine-game losing streak, the Jets have been among the NHL's best teams, going six straight wins. The Jets have found ways to win even when goaltending hasn't been adequate, as in Skinner's most recent outing, when he allowed three goals on eight shots (.625 SV%) before being pulled, rallying the team to a 5-4 shootout win over the Chicago Blackhawks. The 28-year-old Skinner has a 3.43 GAA and .864 SV% in his last five appearances (4-0-0). The Jets enter Tuesday's game as +119 home underdogs against an Ottawa Senators team that is 4-0-1 in their last five games.

away.name: Jake Oettinger
away.news: Oettinger was stellar in his most recent game, stopping all 22 shots he faced to lead a 2-0 shutout win over the Buffalo Sabres. That said, the 27-year-old Oettinger has been wildly inconsistent this season. Oettinger leads the NHL with four shutouts, but has a sub- .900 SV% in seven of 15 games this season (10-4-1). The Stars enter Tuesday's game as +109 road underdogs against a Vegas Golden Knights team coming off a disappointing 6-3 loss to the Vancouver Canucks.

home.name: Adin Hill
home.news: The Golden Knights have had a liberal goalie rotation in recent weeks and will continue that trend on Tuesday, turning to Adin Hill. After posting a career-worst 3.04 GAA and .871 SV% in 27 games last season (10-9-6), Hill has bounced back, posting a 2.47 GAA and .908 SV% in 10 games (7-2-1). He has a 1.62 GAA and a .943 SV% in his last three games (2-0-1). The Golden Knights enter Thursday's game as -130 home favourites against the Dallas Stars, who are 5-1-1 in their last seven games.

away.name: Dustin Wolf
away.news: Before being sidelined with a lower-body injury, Devin Cooley owned the crease in Calgary, but he has struggled since returning. Meanwhile, Dustin Wolf seems to have found his game during Cooley's absence. The 25-year-old Wolf was excellent in his most recent outing, saving 29 of 31 shots (.935 SV%) in a 3-2 win over the Los Angeles Kings. In his last five games (3-1-1), Wolf has a solid 2.22 GAA and a .920 SV%. The Flames enter Tuesday's game as +116 road underdogs against the San Jose Sharks, whom they defeated 2-1 earlier this month.

home.name: Yaroslav Askarov
home.news: Askarov had a rough performance in his previous outing, allowing five goals on 32 shots (.844 SV%), but managed to win 6-5 in a shootout over the Utah Mammoth. The 24-year-old Russian goalie has had an inconsistent season. In 15 games this season (6-8-1), Askarov has allowed four or more goals six times, but has allowed two or fewer seven times. The Sharks enter Tuesday's game as -127 home favourites against a Calgary Flames team coming off a 6-1 loss to the Anaheim Ducks.
